steps.content: As expected, the Mania rift spits Norma out once again.
The pesky monkeys are gone. Her monitoring model lies amid cotton-candy-like blossoms. Norma swiftly calibrates it to collect data, then plants another beacon to stabilize this Mania-distorted area.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: This data alone isn't sufficient. Combined with the readings from the <color=#fb9259>recorder</color> on the Chief's end, I should be able to reach some conclusions.
Once the data synchronizes, every stranded person is pinpointed. Apart from the Chief, all those swept into this Mania field are Sinners.
At least no innocent civilians blundered in. Norma cocks an eyebrow.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: If my hypothesis holds, that anomalous space is undoubtedly the Bureau. The deviation in Sinner abilities, the weakening of Mania creatures—all of it stems from a source distorting the rules of reality.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Which raises the question... which space is the real one?
Norma taps at the keyboard, trying to locate the source of the distorted Mania field, but warning messages flash onto the screen once more.
With the beacon's help, Norma can now roughly correlate this world's numerical data with the Bureau's internal layout.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Dwelling on that question won't help... The priority is getting this information back.
She opens the communication terminal, but the screen still shows nothing but static.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Wait, there's another possibility...
She pulls up the Bureau map she requested when installing the monitoring models and compares it against the terrain of this anomalous space.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: What if both spaces are real, interacting with and feeding back into each other?
On the screen, the two maps begin to overlap. She quickly locks onto a set of coordinates.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Found it. The way to transmit information.
After successfully transmitting the message, Norma lets out a heavy sigh. This space has all but shattered every rule she has believed in until now.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: This is like... trying to calibrate a scale with a broken set of weights.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Even if the numbers add up, the process is utterly inelegant.

She slides her glasses back on, her gaze turning professionally cold behind the lenses. She scans the area. The beacons she'd tagged as stable are now humming faintly, their readings pulsing at erratic frequencies.
Her fingers fly across the keyboard as she hunts for the source of the rule-rewriting force. Amid the weaving threads of data, a minuscule but deeply oppressive black dot flickers by.
It's no Mania creature, no lingering Sinner energy. It's more like a pair of eyes... overseeing the entire chessboard.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Of course. Information flows both ways. Transmitting that message was bound to attract attention.

steps.speaker: Norma
steps.content: Since you're so eager to reveal your ugly side, I see no reason to keep indulging these absurd monkeys.
Norma leaves. In her wake, a thin rift splits the sky. That dark figure, the one that once lurked behind her, gathers itself again, moving to strike at the order she just brought to this space...
Rules... interesting... I will make sure you never return...
